name: Seashell Pink
lede: Seashell Pink is a pale yellowish pink that Maerz and Paul trace to 1901, and in our archive it concentrates heavily in the work of a single painter, Xugu.

sections.title: A pale pink among many pale pinks
sections.body:
Ridgway's 1912 plates give Seashell Pink at hue 11′, tone f, on plate XIV, and the Inter-Society Color Council's 1955 census files it, in block 28, as a pale yellowish pink, Munsell 6.0YR 8.7/3.1 [1]. Maerz and Paul trace the name to 1901, on their plate 10 A 4 [1].

ColorHub's library places its nearest neighbor at [[desert-sand]], about 3.2 units away, with [[alabaster]] and [[unbleached-silk]] almost as close [1]. *Seashell* joins a small family of shell-named pinks, including [[shell-pink]], a cooler, grayer cousin rather than a twin [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds Seashell Pink in 203 of 23,781 paintings, about 0.9 percent, almost always as a highlight [2]. It peaks around 1900, twice its average rate, and concentrates heavily in one painter's hand: Xugu carries it in 7 of his 16 dated works [2]. Chinese paintings carry it nearly six times the archive's base rate, with Nepal and India also above average [2]. It shares canvases with [[peach]] far more than chance alone predicts, and with [[ecru]] and [[beige]] as well [2]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, read as screen colors, not pigment identifications[2].
